note: C-37075, Organizational Churn: A Roll of the Dice. 21 pages, 13 measured regions on 9 pages. Eleven printed exhibits (nine figures + two tables) plus one page-1 header rule excluded. Every figure in this paper is a MATLAB export; the caption is printed BELOW the drawing in all eleven cases. Two traps: (1) layout filed Figure 6 under '296 Churn Rate=35%', which is a y-axis tick of the chart itself, not a heading - place is overridden to 5.4 Task 4; (2) Figure 8 is one figure in four labelled panels (a)-(d) but the extractor measured two rows, so it is recorded as two rows of two panels each, the same way Figure 3 was recorded in P-C-2015-33572. Caption noun does not decide family: 'Churn Rates of Different Levels' is a box plot, not a bar chart, and 'Budget Calculation' is two line panels.
rules: A caption below the drawing is the default in this paper: eleven of eleven exhibits print their caption under the object, so caption.position below carries no information here and must be read together with the region's own page_zone - a caption at the top of a crop belongs to whatever is above it [caption.position].

The caption noun does not name the family: 'Churn Rates of Different Levels' is an eight-box box plot, 'Budget Calculation' is two line panels, and 'HR health in different periods' is an organisation chart. Decide the family from the marks in the crop, then use the caption only for the title [geometry.family].

A MATLAB figure with several panels in one measured region is ONE row with panel_count set to what is inside that region and panel_layout spelling the arrangement - column of 3 for Figures 4 and 6, 1x2 for Figures 5 and 8's rows, 2x2 for Figure 7 - and never several rows each claiming one panel of it [geometry.panel_count].

When the extractor splits one composite into two regions, both rows are real exhibits and both carry the identical caption and family; the note says which labelled panels the row holds. Figure 8 is (a)(b) on one row and (c)(d) on the next [caption.verbatim].

Legend placement follows where the box is drawn, not where the series are explained: Figure 4's only key sits inside its first panel, Figure 6's single key sits outside the top-right corner above the first panel's axes, and Figures 5, 7, 8 and 9 explain colour or series in printed panel titles or in the caption sentence and therefore have legend none [geometry.legend].

shared_axes turns on only when the panels share the same measured quantity: Figures 5, 6 and 9 share a single x axis (time, time, α), while Figure 4's three panels plot three different x quantities and stays false even though the panels are stacked [geometry.shared_axes].

An axis tick can be promoted to a heading by the layout pass - Figure 6 was filed under '296 Churn Rate=35%'. When the alleged heading is a number-and-label pair in the chart's own tick sequence, override place to the real numbered heading and keep section_kind from that heading [place.section_path].

No figure in this paper prints a data value on the drawing: every panel runs on axis ticks only, so printed_numbers and data_labels are false throughout, and any number quoted in the notes is a body-text read, not a pixel read [geometry.printed_numbers].

A table with rules above the header, under the header and at the bottom and no vertical rules is booktabs, while the same paper's allocation table draws vertical rules between every column and boxes the grid, which is boxed; zebra shading appears in neither [table.rule_style].

Merged stub cells are the norm in both tables here: Table 1 merges the Tier column across seven-row and nine-row blocks and carries a diagonal split header, Table 2 merges each strategy name across its Staff Number and Increase(%) pair, so merged_cells true does not imply a broken grid [table.merged_cells].

An exhibit can be named for the first time AFTER it appears: Table 2 is printed on p16 and only named in 'From Table 2, we can easily compare different promotion strategies' on p17, which leaves lead_pages at -1. Record the negative gap rather than inventing a lead on the table's own page [mention.lead_pages].

A sentence that wraps across lines is quoted as consecutive whole text-layer lines, so a lead can begin mid-clause when the naming sentence starts at the end of a printed line; the quote stays a verbatim substring of the page, which is what the census verifies, and read_sentences records how many sentences were read [mention.lead_sentence].
